grammar_concept.title: Relative Clauses: who, which, that
grammar_concept.rule: Use "who" for people, "which" for things, and "that" for either, to add extra information about a noun without starting a new sentence.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Uma oração relativa junta duas frases numa só, evitando repetir o substantivo: em vez de "I have a friend. My friend lives in London.", dizemos "I have a friend who lives in London."
grammar_concept.example: The woman who called you is my sister. This is the book that I told you about.
grammar_concept.example_translation: A mulher que te ligou é minha irmã. Este é o livro de que te falei.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português falado é comum repetir o pronome depois da oração relativa ("A mulher que ela ligou..."). Em inglês isso está errado: a oração relativa já substitui completamente o pronome — nunca se repete o sujeito ou objeto. "The woman who she called you" está incorreto; o correto é "The woman who called you", sem "she" a mais.
grammar_concept.correction: "Who"/"which"/"that" substituem completamente o sujeito ou objeto — nunca use outro pronome a seguir dentro da mesma oração relativa. "Who" para pessoas, "which" para coisas, "that" pode substituir os dois em orações relativas essenciais (sem vírgulas).
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A descrever alguém: "That's the man who fixed my car last week."

example_sentences: She's a colleague who I really trust.

vocabulary.definition_en: a person who owns and rents out a property
example_sentences: My landlord is the person who fixed the heating.
A stranger who helped me pick up my bags didn't even give his name.

exercises.prompt: Complete: The woman ___ called you is my sister.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "which" para pessoas, ou repetir "she" a mais, são erros comuns.

correct_answer: This is the book that I told you about.
distractors: This is the book that I told you about it.
This is the book which I told you it.
This is the book I told you about it.
exercises.explanation: Não se repete "it" depois da oração relativa — já está implícito em "that".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Repetir o pronome ("about it") no fim é um erro muito comum de transferência do português falado.

correct_answer: a person who owns and rents out a property
distractors: a person who rents a flat (the tenant)
exercises.explanation: "Landlord" é o dono do imóvel; quem aluga e vive lá é o "tenant".

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the landlord do?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "My landlord is the person who fixed the heating last week."
exercises.transcript: My landlord is the person who fixed the heating last week. He's actually a really nice guy.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "I have a colleague who speaks four languages. She's the person who helped me with the translation last month." What did the colleague help with?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "helped me with the translation".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Este é o colega que me ajudou ontem."
correct_answer: This is the colleague who helped me yesterday.
This is the colleague that helped me yesterday.
exercises.explanation: "Who"/"that" substituem completamente o sujeito da oração relativa.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Acrescentar "he" a mais ("who he helped me") é o erro mais comum nesta frase.

steps.content: Relative clauses are usually said as one continuous phrase with the noun they describe, with no pause before "who"/"which"/"that": "the woman who called" — not "the woman... who called".

steps.prompt: Describe 3 people in your life using relative clauses (a colleague who..., a friend who..., a neighbour who...).
Write 5 sentences describing people or things you know, using "who", "which" or "that".
